title: A 0.52mJ/Frame 107fps Super-Resolution Processor Exploiting Pseudo-FP6 Sparsity for Mobile Applications
problem: CNN-based super-resolution (SRCNN) for mobile applications suffers from three challenges: (1) large on-chip memory for multi-dimensional overlapping regions in layer-fusion limits external-bandwidth reduction, (2) traditional low-bit-width quantization degrades image quality, requiring novel high-dynamic-range computation, (3) deconvolution accounts for large workload but reusing convolution datapath creates redundant calculations.
motivation: Mobile gaming, video, and photography demand efficient super-resolution hardware that minimizes battery drain and latency.
method: Mobile super-resolution processor using pseudo-FP6 (low-bit-width high-dynamic-range) quantization, memory-optimized layer-fusion dataflow minimizing overlapping-region buffering, and efficient deconvolution processing, achieving 0.52mJ/frame at 107fps.
key_novelty: Pseudo-FP6 format enabling high dynamic range with low bit-width, combined with optimized dataflow reducing multi-dimensional overlapping-region memory footprint.
contributions: Pseudo-FP6 quantization maintaining image quality vs. traditional low-bit approaches
Memory-optimized layer-fusion reducing external-memory access and redundant deconvolution calculations
limitations: Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and perceptual quality metrics not provided; scaling to higher-resolution inputs not discussed.
